out.reviewText: . / EASILY CONFUSED WITH / MugwortArtemisia vulgaris / Mugwort commonly has noticeably pale or silvery-white leaf undersides; ragweed foliage is not strongly white beneath. / GoldenrodSolidago canadensis / Goldenrod is often blamed for ragweed pollen allergy, but goldenrod carries conspicuous yellow flower clusters and ragweed does not. / TYPICAL HABITAT / Disturbed soils, roadsides, vacant lots, gardens, crop fields and open waste places. / THIS MATCHES MY PLANT / I’m not sure yet / Log it only if you met this plant outdoors. / HERBAL SAFETY / An identification from a photograph is a starting point, not proof. / For education only — not medical advice. / Read full safety information → / FORAGING SAFETY: Avoid eating or using plants from areas that may have been treated with pesticides, herbicides, or other chemicals. If you’re unsure whether an area was sprayed, don’t consume the plant.
